items.stem: A 52-year-old woman presents with acute left-sided loin to groin pain on a background of polyuria and generalized skeletal aches. On examination, she has a serum calcium of 3.1 mmol/L with a raised parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentration of 150 ng/L. A plain kidney, ureter and bladder (KUB) film shows a stone in the left ureter. Which of the following types of renal stone is most likely to be the culprit in this case?
items.explanation: The most common form of renal stone is from calcium oxalate, occurring in 80% of cases. These stones can sometimes be seen on plain KUB X-ray films. Calcium phosphate stones are generally associated with primary hyperparathyroidism as in this case (high PTH and high calcium levels). Uric acid forms 10% of cases and produces radiolucent stones.

items.stem: A 46-year-old female presents to the general surgical clinic with a 9-week history of a left-sided neck lump. Following thorough investigation and discussion at the local multidisciplinary meeting, a hemithyroidectomy is performed. The lesion histologically represents a follicular carcinoma. Which of the following statements regarding follicular carcinoma is correct?
options: Radiation exposure is a risk factor for its development.
It has a prevalence of approximately 5% of thyroid carcinomas.
It has a 5-year survival rate of approximately 70%.
It is diagnosed by ultrasound and fine-needle aspiration cytology.
items.answer_text: It has a 5-year survival rate of approximately 70%.
items.explanation: Follicular carcinoma is the second most common carcinoma of the thyroid, with a prevalence of approximately 15% (following papillary carcinoma, with a prevalence of approximately 80%). Spread is typically haematogenous; lymphatic spread is unusual. It has a 5-year survival rate of approximately 70%. It is diagnosed by ultrasound and excision biopsy to demonstrate extracapsular spread; fine-needle aspiration cytology is unable to differentiate between follicular carcinoma and change follicular adenoma.
